mainTopic: The metal lamp in רבי עקיבא's statement, the Torah-level impurity of liquids, and the source of רבי מאיר's ruling
overview: The amud finishes רב יהודה's explanation of רבי עקיבא's statement in the משנה. From the פסוק 'בחלל חרב', a metal vessel takes on the level of the impurity it touches, so a metal lamp that touched a טמא מת becomes an אב הטומאה. That turns the oil from a שלישי into a ראשון. The גמרא asks why רב יהודה needed metal, since an earthenware lamp would still teach something new: oil that was only פסול becoming טמא. רבא answers that the משנה's wording forced him. The משנה says 'טמא מת' rather than the more common שרץ, and only for metal does that difference matter. רבא then proves that רבי עקיבא holds that the power of impure liquids to make other things impure is דאורייתא. If it were only rabbinic, even a ראשון or שני would make liquids a תחלה, and no אב הטומאה would be needed. Finally, the גמרא asks whose words רבי מאיר learned from when he allowed burning pure and impure תרומה together. It shows that neither רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים nor רבי עקיבא fits, and it suggests that רבי מאיר's 'pure' item is pure only by Torah law. That suggestion is examined on the next amud.

steps.title: A metal vessel is like the corpse, so the lamp is a primary source of impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's explanation ends with its source. From 'בחלל חרב', a sword (metal) is treated like the corpse itself, so the metal lamp becomes an אב הטומאה. This shows that רבי עקיבא allows turning a שלישי into a ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'By one slain with a sword.' A sword is like the slain corpse. So the lamp becomes an אב הטומאה, and רבי עקיבא holds that it is permitted to make a third-degree item into a first-degree item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יהודה's explanation of the metal lamp by giving his source from the פסוק and stating what it proves about רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a vessel that touches a person who touched a corpse becomes only a ראשון. Metal is different: based on 'חרב הרי הוא כחלל', metal takes on the same level as what it touched, so the lamp becomes an אב הטומאה. The oil, which was a שלישי from touching a טבול יום, now becomes a ראשון. That is a two-level jump, and רבי עקיבא allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By one slain with a sword' (במדבר יט:טז), the source that metal takes on corpse-level impurity
A sword (metal vessel) is like the corpse itself
A primary source of impurity, which makes what it touches a ראשון

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sword is literally a corpse. The rule only means that a metal vessel takes on the same level of impurity as the source it touched. Because of this, the lamp becomes an אב הטומאה instead of just a ראשון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key to the whole explanation. Only a metal lamp can be an אב הטומאה, and only an אב הטומאה can turn the oil into a ראשון.

phrases.english: 'By one slain with a sword.'
A sword is like the slain corpse.
phrases.notes: A metal vessel takes on the impurity level of its source

phrases.english: And so the lamp becomes a primary source of impurity,
and he (רבי עקיבא) holds that it is permitted to make a third-degree item into a first-degree item.
phrases.notes: The oil goes from שלישי to ראשון

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּחֲלַל חֶרֶב חֶרֶב הֲרֵי הוּא כֶּחָלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's explanation, which began on the previous amud, that the lamp is made of metal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A metal lamp that touched a טמא מת becomes an אב הטומאה. רבי עקיבא therefore permits turning a שלישי into a ראשון.

steps.title: Why not say the lamp is earthenware?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what forced רב יהודה to say the lamp is metal. He could have said it is an earthenware lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: What forced רב יהודה to explain the case as a metal lamp? Let him explain it as an earthenware lamp!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. Why did he insist on a metal lamp when a simple clay lamp seems to work just as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earthenware lamp that touches a טמא מת becomes only a ראשון, not an אב. The oil would then go from שלישי to שני, which is just one level. The question is why רב יהודה chose the more extreme metal case when a milder one seems available.

keyTerms.meaning: To set the case up as

phrases.english: And what forced Rav Yehuda
to set up the case as a metal lamp?
Let him set it up as an earthenware lamp!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setup that רב יהודה just gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's choice of a metal lamp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler case, an earthenware lamp, seems possible, so there is no clear reason to insist on metal.

steps.title: An earthenware lamp would still show what רבי עקיבא added
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers in advance the objection that an earthenware lamp would leave nothing new in רבי עקיבא's statement. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים spoke about something already טמא becoming more טמא. רבי עקיבא would be adding a case where oil that was only פסול becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did רבי עקיבא 'add'? That there, the case was impure plus impure, while here, it is disqualified becoming impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge continues. The גמרא heads off an expected reply by showing that even with an earthenware lamp, רבי עקיבא's 'addition' still teaches something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא allowed meat that was already טמא to be burned with meat that was more טמא. With an earthenware lamp, the oil goes from שלישי, which is only פסול, to שני, which is actually טמא. Turning a merely disqualified item into an impure one is a real new point. So metal does not seem necessary to explain the word 'הוסיף'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Added' — רבי עקיבא added a new teaching beyond רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים
Impure plus impure: something already impure becoming more impure
Disqualified becoming impure: something that was only invalid becoming able to spread impurity
There (רבי חנינא's case) / here (רבי עקיבא's case)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is still part of the question, not the גמרא's answer. It explains why an earthenware lamp would not leave רבי עקיבא's 'addition' empty.

phrases.english: And what would 'he added' mean?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is answering ahead of time the objection that, with earthenware, he wouldn't be adding anything new.

phrases.english: That there, it was impure with impure,
phrases.notes: 'There' means רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים's case about the meat.

phrases.english: while here it is disqualified becoming impure!
phrases.notes: The oil goes from שלישי (פסול) to שני (טמא)

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי הוֹסִיף דְּאִילּוּ הָתָם טָמֵא וְטָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge from step 2 by showing that the earthenware reading still gives meaning to 'הוסיף'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a metal lamp to explain רבי עקיבא's addition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even an earthenware lamp creates a new point, פסול becoming טמא, so metal is unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא: the wording of the משנה pushed רב יהודה to say metal
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה's wording bothered רב יהודה. Why does it say the lamp became impure through a טמא מת and not simply through a שרץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה was difficult for him. Why does it specifically teach 'a lamp that became impure through one impure from a corpse'? Let it teach 'a lamp that became impure through a שרץ'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to answer the question of step 2 by revealing what bothered רב יהודה: an unusual detail in the משנה's wording. The full answer continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ is a common אב הטומאה. If the משנה only wanted an earthenware lamp that is a ראשון, a שרץ would make that happen just as well. Choosing טמא מת points to the special rule of 'חרב הרי הוא כחלל', which only applies to metal, so the lamp itself becomes an אב. That is why רב יהודה said the lamp is metal.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה was difficult for him; its wording forced his reading
Someone who became impure from a corpse
A creeping creature, a common אב הטומאה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic way the גמרא reads a משנה: an unusual or less common detail must have a reason. Here that reason is the special metal rule.

phrases.english: Rava said: The mishna was difficult for him:
Why specifically does it teach
'a lamp that became impure through one impure from a corpse'?
Let it teach 'that became impure through a creeping creature'!
phrases.notes: A שרץ is a more common אב הטומאה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 2 and 3 by pointing to the משנה's wording as רב יהודה's motive.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual precision: the משנה's unusual choice of טמא מת points to metal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An earthenware lamp would work, since it still teaches פסול becoming טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mention of טמא מת instead of the more common שרץ signals the metal rule of 'חרב הרי הוא כחלל'. That is why רב יהודה said the lamp is metal (completed next).

steps.title: Only metal is affected differently by a corpse than by a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רבא completes his answer. The only material that becomes more impure from a טמא מת than from a שרץ is metal, so רב יהודה said the lamp was metal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what kind of item becomes impure differently from a corpse than from a שרץ? You must say it is metal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer to the question of why רב יהודה said the lamp was made of metal. The משנה said 'טמא מת' instead of 'שרץ', and only metal makes that difference matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earthenware lamp would become a ראשון whether it touched a שרץ or a טמא מת, so the משנה would have no reason to mention a corpse. A metal item that touches a corpse becomes an אב הטומאה, based on חרב כחלל. Because the משנה chose the words 'טמא מת', the lamp must be metal.

keyTerms.meaning: Its impurity is different (depending on the source)
You must say (the only possible answer is)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's choice of 'טמא מת' over 'שרץ' proves the lamp is metal. Only metal becomes an אב הטומאה through contact with a corpse.

phrases.english: Rather: what is the item
whose impurity is different
between impurity from a corpse and from a creeping animal?
You must say: this is metal.
phrases.notes: Metal touching a corpse (or someone who touched one) becomes an אב הטומאה. Metal touching a שרץ becomes only a ראשון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer that began in Step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamp could have been earthenware
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'טמא מת' only make a difference for metal, so the lamp must be metal

steps.title: רבא's conclusion that liquid impurity spreading to others is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from רבי עקיבא's case that the power of impure liquids to make other things impure is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn from this that רבי עקיבא holds that the impurity of liquids, in making other things impure, is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the lamp is understood, רבא draws a new halachic conclusion about רבי עקיבא's view. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some תנאים hold that liquids can pass on impurity to other items only by rabbinic decree. רבא says רבי עקיבא disagrees and holds that this power comes from the Torah. This is a new rule learned from the case of the oil and the lamp.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not asking whether liquids themselves can become impure. He is asking whether their power to pass impurity on to OTHER things is from the Torah.

phrases.english: Rava said: learn from this
that Rabbi Akiva holds:
the impurity of liquids, to make others impure,
is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קָסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion that the lamp is metal to draw a new rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, impure liquids make other things impure on a Torah level

steps.title: The lamp must add something beyond disqualifying the oil
steps.stepSummary: Proof: the oil was already פסול. So the lamp must be giving it the Torah-level power to make other things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think it is only rabbinic: what does this lamp accomplish for this oil? If it is to make the oil itself פסול, it is already פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his conclusion. He asks what the lamp adds to the oil, given that the oil was already disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil was already a שלישי, which is פסול. Touching the lamp cannot be teaching us that the oil becomes פסול, because it already is. The lamp's contribution must be making the oil a ראשון that can spread impurity to others, and רבא assumes this is a Torah-level effect.

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that it is rabbinic,
now, this lamp —
what does it accomplish for this oil?
If to disqualify the oil itself —
it is already disqualified!
phrases.notes: The oil was made פסול earlier by a טבול יום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim made in Step 6
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא holds that liquids spreading impurity to others is דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The lamp must add something to oil that was already פסול

steps.title: Maybe the oil's new power is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: perhaps the lamp gives the oil the power to make others impure only by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps it makes others impure only by rabbinic law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. It suggests the lamp might add only a rabbinic-level power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא proved that the lamp adds something. He did not prove that what it adds is from the Torah. The challenge says the oil's new ability to make others impure might be only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: From where do you know?
Perhaps it is to make others impure by rabbinic law.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's conclusion that the added power is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lamp could add a rabbinic power just as well as a Torah power

steps.title: If it were rabbinic, an אב הטומאה would not be needed
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected. By rabbinic law, even a ראשון or שני makes liquids a תחלה, so an אב הטומאה would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were rabbinic, why specifically an אב הטומאה? Even with a ראשון or a שני, the oil would also become a תחלה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. רבי עקיבא's case only makes sense if the effect is from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By rabbinic decree, liquids that touch anything impure, even a שני, become a תחלה (first level). If רבי עקיבא only meant a rabbinic effect, he would not need a lamp that is an אב הטומאה. Since he specifically used an אב הטומאה, the effect must be דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: First and second levels of impurity
'First' level — for liquids, it means a ראשון

steps.whatToRemember: Mentioning an אב הטומאה only makes sense on a Torah level. By rabbinic law, any impure item already makes liquids a תחלה.

phrases.english: If it is rabbinic,
why specifically through a primary source of impurity?
Even through a first or second degree, too,
it would become first-degree!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדְּרַבָּנַן, מַאי אִירְיָא בְּאַב הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 8 and confirms רבא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that רבי עקיבא meant only a rabbinic effect
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By rabbinic law, no אב הטומאה is needed to make liquids a תחלה

steps.title: The משנה that anything disqualifying תרומה makes liquids a תחלה
steps.stepSummary: The source for the rabbinic rule: anything that disqualifies תרומה makes liquids a תחלה, except a טבול יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: anything that disqualifies תרומה makes liquids impure so that they become a תחלה, except a טבול יום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source for the rule it used in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a שני, which only disqualifies תרומה, turns liquids into a ראשון by rabbinic decree. The single exception is a טבול יום. This explains why the oil in רבי עקיבא's case was only פסול: a טבול יום had touched it.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed today but the sun has not yet set

steps.whyThisMatters: The טבול יום exception is exactly why the oil in רבי עקיבא's case stayed a שלישי. It also shows why the lamp was needed to raise the oil to a ראשון on a Torah level.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Anything that disqualifies teruma
makes liquids impure so they become first-degree,
except for one who immersed that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the rule used in Step 9
steps.raayaObject: By rabbinic law, even a ראשון or שני makes liquids a תחלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה: כל הפוסל את התרומה מטמא משקין להיות תחלה חוץ מטבול יום

steps.title: So the impurity of liquids is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The rabbinic reading was pushed away, so the גמרא concludes that liquids make other things impure מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that it is Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבא's argument. Since the 'rabbinic only' idea was rejected, the conclusion stands that liquids pass on impurity by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 we saw that by rabbinic law, even a ראשון or שני makes liquids a תחלה. So if רבי עקיבא needed an אב הטומאה, the lamp must be adding a Torah-level power. That means the power of liquids to make other things impure is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא's reading of רבי עקיבא, the power of impure liquids to make other things impure is דאורייתא, not just דרבנן.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it
that it is Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion after the rabbinic option was rejected in steps 9 and 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The power of liquids to make other things impure is דאורייתא.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's line in the משנה: 'From their words we learned…', which allows burning pure and impure תרומה together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: From their words we learned, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new line from the משנה to study it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says that from the words of earlier חכמים we can learn that pure תרומה may be burned together with impure תרומה on ערב פסח. The phrase 'from their words' leaves open which earlier statement he is building on.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
From their words we learned, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, moving from רבי עקיבא's case to רבי מאיר's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר learns from earlier חכמים that pure and impure תרומה may be burned together on ערב פסח.

steps.title: Whose words did רבי מאיר learn from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier statement רבי מאיר is referring to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: who are 'they' in 'from their words'? This sets up a test of possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two earlier rulings that could be the source: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים and רבי עקיבא. The גמרא wants to know which one matches רבי מאיר's case.

phrases.english: From whose words?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the statement quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier ruling, רבי חנינא's or רבי עקיבא's, is the basis for רבי מאיר's inference.

steps.title: Not from רבי חנינא, because his case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים as the source but rejects it. He burned impure with impure, while רבי מאיר burns pure with impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is from the words of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, are the cases alike? There it is impure and impure. Here it is pure and impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible source and right away shows that it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא allowed meat that was already impure, a little, to be burned with meat that is more impure. Both items were already טמא. רבי מאיר makes a pure item impure, which is a much bigger step, so it cannot be learned from רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be tested)
Are they alike? (usually means: no, they are not)

phrases.english: If you say, from the words of
Rabbi Chanina, the deputy High Priest,
is it comparable?
There it is impure and impure,
here it is pure and impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא מִדִּבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים, מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 13 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי חנינא as the source of רבי מאיר's inference.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי חנינא's case involves two items that are both טמא. רבי מאיר's case makes a טהור item impure.

steps.title: Not from רבי עקיבא either, because his case is also different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא then suggests רבי עקיבא as the source but rejects it too. His case is פסול with impure, not pure with impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from the words of רבי עקיבא. Are the cases alike? There it is disqualified and impure. Here it is pure and impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second possible source, and that one does not fit either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא allowed oil that was already פסול (made unfit by a טבול יום) to become טמא in an impure lamp. Even though the oil was not fully impure, it was already damaged. In רבי מאיר's case the תרומה is fully טהור, so the gap is still too big.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (moving to the next option)
Disqualified: unfit, but does not make other things impure

steps.confusionAlert: פָּסוּל is not the same as טָמֵא. A פסול item is unfit, but it is not impure enough to pass impurity on. That is why it sits 'between' טהור and טמא.

phrases.english: But rather, from the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Is it comparable?
There it is disqualified and impure,
here it is pure and impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מִדִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי חנינא is rejected, the גמרא tests רבי עקיבא and rejects him too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא as a direct source of רבי מאיר's inference.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא's oil was already פסול. רבי מאיר's תרומה is fully טהור.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי חנינא's less-impure meat was impure only rabbinically
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר reads the משנה of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים as dealing with an אב הטומאה from the Torah and a ולד הטומאה that is impure only מדרבנן. That ולד is fully pure by Torah law, so רבי חנינא's case is really pure with impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that רבי מאיר holds that our משנה is about an אב הטומאה that is Torah-level and a ולד הטומאה that is rabbinic, which by Torah law is completely pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to find רבי מאיר's source after all: in רבי חנינא's case, the less-impure meat was impure only by rabbinic law, so by Torah law it was pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 rejected רבי חנינא because his case seemed to be impure with impure. If the lesser meat, a ולד הטומאה, was impure only מדרבנן, then by Torah law it was fully pure, and רבי חנינא's case becomes Torah-pure with impure, just like רבי מאיר's. The word נימא shows this is only a suggestion, and the גמרא tests it on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (a suggestion that may be tested)
He holds / is of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The item that is 'pure by Torah law' here is the less-impure meat in רבי חנינא's case, not the pure תרומה in רבי מאיר's ruling. The suggestion reinterprets the source case, not רבי מאיר's own case.

phrases.english: Let us say Rabbi Meir holds
that our mishna is about a Torah-level primary source of impurity
phrases.notes: 'The משנה' here means רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים's ruling about the meat.

phrases.english: and a rabbinic-level secondary impurity,
which by Torah law is completely pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the rejection in step 14 by reinterpreting רבי חנינא's case so that it becomes Torah-pure with impure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's case is impure with impure, so it cannot be רבי מאיר's source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lesser item in רבי חנינא's case is a rabbinic ולד הטומאה, fully pure by Torah law, so רבי מאיר could learn pure-with-impure from it. The suggestion is tested on the next amud.
